case_prompt:
<case_prompt>
A patient presents with intermittent fever spikes exceeding 38°C, shivering, and abdominal pain occurring predominantly in the evenings. Broad-spectrum empiric intravenous antimicrobial therapy with piperacillin/tazobactam is initiated for suspected acute intra-abdominal infection. Peripheral blood count demonstrates a normal absolute neutrophil count of 7.07 x 10^9/L, monocytosis of 0.98 x 10^9/L, and lymphopenia of 0.86 x 10^9/L. Serum tests of renal and hepatic function, as well as coagulation parameters, are within normal reference ranges. Microbiological surveillance samples from blood, urine, tonsils, and nasal mucosa are all negative. Transthoracic echocardiography is normal without intracardiac vegetations.
</case_prompt>

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Acute Bacterial Intra-abdominal Sepsis / Suppurative Thrombophlebitis
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: High-grade fever spikes, chills, and abdominal pain strongly suggested acute bacterial infection warranting empiric piperacillin/tazobactam; however, no bacterial infection was proven and systemic microbiological cultures remained sterile.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Although no infection was proved, the infectious disease specialist indicated antibiotics (piperacillin/tazobactam i.v.) to treat the symptoms.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the combination of rigors, spiking fevers, and extensive caval thrombosis; ruled out by negative blood cultures and normal echocardiography.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: To exclude intracardiac dissemination, echocardiography was performed with normal results.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Advanced cross-sectional abdominal imaging (ultrasonography, CT, and MRI) revealing massive reactivation of echinococcosis in the right retroperitoneum and suprarenal IVC, almost complete obturation of the IVC and common iliac veins by non-enhancing cystic material, and enlargement of a hepatic hydatid cyst to 39 mm.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Additional examinations (ultrasonography of the abdomen, CT scans of the head, chest and abdomen, MRI examination of the abdomen) showed a massive reactivation of echinococcosis in the abdominal area (right retroperineum, the suprarenal part of the IVC) (Figure 2). The IVC and common iliac veins bilaterally were nearly completely obturated by hyperintense material on native T1 fat saturated sequence (Figure 3) and after contrast medium administration without an enhancement (Figures 4 and 5), possibly CE, as suggested by the radiologist.

editor_comments: Admission breakpoint placed prior to advanced MRI/CT findings revealing echinococcosis reactivation. Zero pathogen spoilers. Direct verbatim quotes in diagnostic reasoning. Audit flags NONE.
